sections.title: The seven cups hold different things
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A dark figure stands in the foreground with a hand extended towards seven golden cups arranged on clouds. At the top are a face, a white-draped form surrounded by red rays, and a snake reaching over a rim. The lower cups contain a tower-like building, colourful jewels, a green wreath and a winged dragon-like creature.

The cups hang among clouds without a table or firm ground, and the figure has not actually taken hold of any of them. Beauty, wealth, honour and unsettling forms appear together, creating temptation and uncertainty. A striking object does not establish that it must correspond to a particular real person. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups07.jpg)

sections.title: The text separates imagination from substantial results
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot connects the visions in the cups with imagination, reflection and contemplation. It specifically notes the absence of permanent or substantial results. Reversed terms include desire, will, determination and a project. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu07.htm)

Selection and testing therefore have historical points of connection, but the practical decision method below is this site’s own work. We do not assign the seven images a single definitive list of life goals or turn them into seven fixed predictions.

sections.title: Upright: Explore, then stop adding options indefinitely
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Imagination has a useful stage. List projects, ways of living or relationships you would like to try without immediately criticising yourself. Yet more options do not automatically mean more opportunities. Possibility begins to take shape when information and conditions are confirmed.

If you keep comparing but never try anything, write down the actual basis of your decision. Do you want a skill, more freedom or other people’s approval? Different needs can give the same option a completely different priority.

sections.title: Reversed: Give determination a checkable task
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The reversal can suggest withdrawing attention from a dazzling array of visions and choosing a direction. Turn the goal into something you can complete this week: speak to someone in the field, make one sample page or confirm enrolment requirements.

Narrowing your choice has risks too. In a rush to end uncertainty, you may ignore unfavourable information. Keep a backup option and decide in advance what evidence would make you reconsider. Stay committed to the underlying need, not necessarily to the first attractive picture of it.

sections.title: Three moments when imagination can run ahead
sections.bodyMarkdown:
When choosing a course, do more than save promotional pages. Check the schedule, actual workload and suitability for your present level, then select one you can try.

If you have many project ideas, use the same criteria to choose one small prototype to test. With a new acquaintance, a single shared interest can easily be expanded into an imagined personality. Ask about real experiences and observe continuing interactions instead of filling the gaps with your wishes.

sections.title: Practice: Pair each wish with evidence
sections.bodyMarkdown: List no more than three options. For each, note its main attraction, the facts you currently know and one condition still to confirm. Investigate the most important unknown. Today, add evidence rather than options, then choose whether to test, set aside or rule something out.

sections.title: A common misreading
sections.bodyMarkdown: The Seven of Cups does not say that wishing brings results, and it cannot diagnose delusions or any mental disorder. A rich imagination is not a fault. The question is whether imagination is being treated as something that has already happened. The card is useful for practising discernment, not mocking dreamers.

articleMarkdown:
# Seven of Cups Meaning: Understand the wish and test one option

In one sentence: Imagination offers many possibilities; action needs fewer, clearer choices.

Card: Seven of Cups  
Rank: VII · RWS Minor Arcana · Cups  
Keywords: Imagination · Temptation · Selection

Upright at a glance: Many options look appealing. Separate what you wish for from what you actually know.  
Reversed at a glance: Your focus may be narrowing. Let one idea meet a real-world test.

The most exciting future in your mind often has no schedule, cost or first step yet. The Seven of Cups allows dreaming while asking which parts exist only in the dream.

## The seven cups hold different things

A dark figure stands in the foreground with a hand extended towards seven golden cups arranged on clouds. At the top are a face, a white-draped form surrounded by red rays, and a snake reaching over a rim. The lower cups contain a tower-like building, colourful jewels, a green wreath and a winged dragon-like creature.

The cups hang among clouds without a table or firm ground, and the figure has not actually taken hold of any of them. Beauty, wealth, honour and unsettling forms appear together, creating temptation and uncertainty. A striking object does not establish that it must correspond to a particular real person. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups07.jpg)

## The text separates imagination from substantial results

The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot connects the visions in the cups with imagination, reflection and contemplation. It specifically notes the absence of permanent or substantial results. Reversed terms include desire, will, determination and a project. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu07.htm)

Selection and testing therefore have historical points of connection, but the practical decision method below is this site’s own work. We do not assign the seven images a single definitive list of life goals or turn them into seven fixed predictions.

## Upright: Explore, then stop adding options indefinitely

Imagination has a useful stage. List projects, ways of living or relationships you would like to try without immediately criticising yourself. Yet more options do not automatically mean more opportunities. Possibility begins to take shape when information and conditions are confirmed.

If you keep comparing but never try anything, write down the actual basis of your decision. Do you want a skill, more freedom or other people’s approval? Different needs can give the same option a completely different priority.

## Reversed: Give determination a checkable task

The reversal can suggest withdrawing attention from a dazzling array of visions and choosing a direction. Turn the goal into something you can complete this week: speak to someone in the field, make one sample page or confirm enrolment requirements.

Narrowing your choice has risks too. In a rush to end uncertainty, you may ignore unfavourable information. Keep a backup option and decide in advance what evidence would make you reconsider. Stay committed to the underlying need, not necessarily to the first attractive picture of it.

## Three moments when imagination can run ahead

When choosing a course, do more than save promotional pages. Check the schedule, actual workload and suitability for your present level, then select one you can try.

If you have many project ideas, use the same criteria to choose one small prototype to test. With a new acquaintance, a single shared interest can easily be expanded into an imagined personality. Ask about real experiences and observe continuing interactions instead of filling the gaps with your wishes.

## Practice: Pair each wish with evidence

List no more than three options. For each, note its main attraction, the facts you currently know and one condition still to confirm. Investigate the most important unknown. Today, add evidence rather than options, then choose whether to test, set aside or rule something out.

## A common misreading

The Seven of Cups does not say that wishing brings results, and it cannot diagnose delusions or any mental disorder. A rich imagination is not a fault. The question is whether imagination is being treated as something that has already happened. The card is useful for practising discernment, not mocking dreamers.

## Read alongside

Knight of Cups: See how an imagined possibility becomes a proposal and action; Nine of Cups: Distinguish hoped-for satisfaction from satisfaction already experienced.

sections.title: 七只杯子没有装着同一种东西
paragraphs: 一个深色背影站在前景，手向前张开，面前云团上排列七只金杯。上方可见一张人脸、罩着白布而周围带红色放射线的形象，以及探出杯沿的蛇。下方杯中分别有高塔般的建筑、彩色珠宝、绿色花环和带翼的龙形怪兽。
杯子悬在云间，没有桌面或落脚的地基，人物也尚未真正拿住任何一只。美丽、财富、荣誉与让人不安的形象并列，制造出诱惑与不确定；不能因为某个物件显眼，就断言它必然对应现实中的某个人。 [查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups07.jpg)

sections.title: 原文把想象与实质成果分开
paragraphs: Waite《塔罗图解之钥》1911 英文转录将这些杯中景象联系到想象、映像与沉思，特意指出其中未显示永久或实质的成果。他给逆位列出的词包括欲望、意志、决心与计划。 [Waite 本牌原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu07.htm)
因此本篇的筛选与验证有历史线索，但具体的决策方法是本站原创。这里不为七个图像指定唯一人生清单，也不把它们解释成七项固定预言。

sections.title: 正位 先允许发散，再停止无限加选项
paragraphs: 想象阶段有用：你可以列出想做的项目、想尝试的生活或希望建立的关系，不急着批评自己。但选项变多并不自动代表机会变多；只有资料和条件得到确认，可能性才开始落地。
当你连续比较却迟迟不试，先写出决定真正依据什么。是想获得技能、更多自由，还是别人的认可？不同需要，会把同一个选项排在完全不同的位置。

sections.title: 逆位 给决心一项可核对的任务
paragraphs: 逆位可读作从令人眼花缭乱的图景中收回注意力，愿意挑一个方向。把目标改写为本周可完成的动作，例如联系一位业内人士、做一页样稿，或查明报名条件。
收拢也有风险：急着结束犹豫时，可能为了确定感而忽略不利信息。可以保留一个备选方案，并先约定什么证据出现后需要改主意。坚持的对象应是需要，而不必是最早那张漂亮想象。

sections.title: 三个很容易被想象带走的时刻
paragraphs: 选择课程时，别只收藏宣传页。先核对时间安排、真实作业量和是否符合现阶段水平，再挑一门可体验的课。
新项目点子很多，就用同一标准选一个小样测试。认识新朋友时，对方的一句共同爱好容易被补成完整性格；多问实际经历、看持续相处，少用自己的愿望填空。

sections.title: 练习 给每个愿望配一条证据
paragraphs: 最多写下三个选项，各列出最吸引你的地方、目前已知的事实和一个待确认条件。选最关键的未知项去查证。今天只新增证据，不再新增选项；随后决定下一步是试做、搁置还是排除。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 圣杯七不表示许愿就能得到，也不能用来诊断妄想或其他心理疾病。丰富的想象并非缺点，问题在于是否把想象当成已经发生的事实。它是一张适合练习辨别的牌，而不是嘲笑做梦者的牌。
